prompt: In 120 to 180 words, explain the bias-variance tradeoff in exactly five numbered points. Include one diagnostic example and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.

turns.assistant_message: The bias-variance tradeoff is a fundamental concept in machine learning that describes the relationship between two types of errors models can make: bias and variance. 1) Bias refers to the error from simplifying assumptions in the learning algorithm; high bias models can miss important relationships in the training data, resulting in a "biased" solution. 2) Variance refers to an overfitting error that occurs when a model is very complex and closely fits the training data. 3) A high variance model will perform well on the training data but poorly on unseen data because it generalizes too much to the noise in the training set.
